- `extension/content.js` is also an accepted-browser live-data bridge: on the reloaded AJIO/Myntra listing tabs it fetches their same-origin listing APIs, selectively enriches incomplete records through product JSON APIs, and posts live results to `/api/browser-bridge/products` on local ports 8787/8788. AJIO uses `/api/search` pagination and Myntra uses multi-sort boundary probes, matching the master extractors; this path does not load product pages. All four `manual_js` master extractors post their completed normalized gold results to the bridge, keyed by retailer identity (AJIO code, Amazon ASIN, Flipkart PID, Myntra ID).
# Aurum Project Context

Updated: 2026-09-01

Use this as a routing index, not as a substitute for reading the owning file before editing it.

Desktop paths described below are relative to `aurum-desktop/` unless explicitly prefixed. Android paths are under `aurum-android/`.

## Runtime

- Node.js 22.5+ ESM application; only runtime dependency is Playwright.
- Main entry point: `aurum-desktop/src/app/server.js`.
- Default bind: `HOST=0.0.0.0`, `PORT=8787`; local working port is commonly 8788.
- Launchers: `aurum-desktop/scripts/run.sh`, OS wrappers in `aurum-desktop/scripts/run-{macos,linux}.sh`, and Windows PowerShell/batch scripts.
- Web frontend: static files under `aurum-desktop/public/`; browser extension under `aurum-desktop/extension/`.
- `aurum-android/` is the native Android 16 app. It is a portable Gradle 9.7.1 / AGP 9.1.0 / compileSdk 36 Kotlin Compose project at version `4.9.22` (`versionCode 40922`); SDK and proxy configuration are local environment concerns and are not stored in repository build files. Android automatic backup is disabled; the bounded in-app archive is the explicit data-transfer path.
- Android persistent state, including Refresh Activity diagnostics, is held in the app-private Room database `aurum.db`; Refresh Activity retains its newest 2,000 entries. Desktop history seeding uses a temporary app-private cache directory and removes it after import. User-directed archive export writes only to the destination selected through Android's document picker.
- Android requests precise location only when Flipkart's WebView asks for it. After the user accepts Android's runtime permission, the active request is granted only to an approved `flipkart.com` origin and is not retained for future page requests; all other retailer WebView geolocation requests are denied.
- Android's loopback bridge treats a client disconnect while writing the HTTP response as normal I/O cleanup, preventing a closed retailer WebView request from crashing the application process.

## Architecture

- `aurum-android/app/`: installable native Compose application with Room products/history/bullion/raw-payload state, an app-private `127.0.0.1:8788` bridge, in-app retailer WebView refreshes, watchlist CRUD, versioned ZIP import/export, persistent settings, WorkManager reminders, direct-HTTP bullion collection, and Tanishq rendered-page collection. Its build packages byte-identical assets from `aurum-desktop/manual_js/` and first-run product seeds from `aurum-desktop/data/products/`; 2,322 source rows deduplicate to 2,305 Room products and never overwrite nonempty device state. The bridge accepts only approved retailer base hosts/subdomains and reports accepted records separately from raw received rows. Product/bullion browser visibility toggles persist, and system back closes Settings/browser screens. Startup and bridge failures are surfaced in-app; WebView main-frame/HTTP/SSL/renderer/script errors advance safely while preserving data. The current app has no foreground service and does not request foreground-service permissions.
- Android mobile UI uses the desktop true-black palette and compact navigation, with purity/search/weight/store/status filtering, quick counts, seven sort modes, coupon-aware product comparison, persistent Deal Radar controls, and a Room-backed blended 24K/22K trend chart with adaptive ₹/g and date/time axes. Deal Radar excludes stale, metadata-incomplete, implausibly cheap, and unavailable product-per-gram observations. Browser is always present as a bottom-navigation destination with job-state tiles, recent store outcomes, and persisted diagnostic activity. Its combined refresh action is explicit; the app-bar Refresh beside Settings remains contextual to Market or Watchlist. Active product WebView runners are mounted once and stay hidden off Browser; selecting Browser expands the same active retailer WebView rather than creating/restarting a second session. Every navigation has timestamped request/load/start/progress/commit/finish/failure diagnostics. Retailer `Not Deliverable`/`Unavailable`/`Out of Stock` name markers are normalized to structured unavailable state; legacy marked rows are excluded from Live/promotion and appear after purchasable rows in the All view under a separate availability section. Product titles open their canonical retailer URLs, and user-facing status labels distinguish `NOT DELIVERABLE`, `NEEDS VERIFICATION`, and `REFRESH FAILED`. Android device screenshots are still required for final physical-layout validation.
- Android Below bullion requires a recent live, deliverable price observation. Structured unavailable, legacy Not Deliverable/Unavailable/Out of Stock, stale, unverified, and failed products remain in their corresponding non-live categories.
- Android Flipkart product-page fallback treats the retailer's explicit `Not deliverable at your location` response as unavailable, matching the unavailable category rather than retaining it as stale.
- After a successful non-AJIO catalogue merge, Android reconciles every non-live store record through the active retailer WebView session. Positive observed prices become live; explicit unavailable/not-deliverable results keep any observed price and become unavailable; ambiguous results retain their prior state.
- The WebView product fallback uses a browser-side settled response slot (`window.__aurumProductFetchResult`) plus bounded Kotlin polling; `evaluateJavascript` alone does not await retailer `fetch()` promises.
- Android post-catalogue missing-product checks fetch retailer endpoints in the already-active store WebView session instead of a separate HTTP client, retaining the same cookies, browser context, and any retailer location state. Ambiguous or Hyperlocal preview responses preserve the stored record.
- Refresh Activity follows newly appended logs only while its scroll panel was last at the bottom. A user who scrolls upward retains their position until they return to the end; collapsed panels are not scrolled.
- Refresh Activity supports independent severity (Errors, Warnings, Info) and store filters. Its count and Copy command apply to the visible filtered log entries; severity remains color-coded in the log text.
- Refresh Activity renders each store label with a stable retailer color, while severity colors continue to identify error, warning, and info messages.
- The visible Browser refresh overlay derives its top and bottom bounds from the measured app-bar and bottom-navigation heights plus system navigation inset, avoiding fixed dp reserves and excess black space across device sizes/densities. Refresh Activity title and Copy/Collapse/Clear remain in one responsive row.
- The active Browser refresh surface omits its redundant title/status header; its dynamic progress line sits directly above retailer tabs, while the detailed title/status remains in the Refresh Activity panel below.
- During an active Browser refresh, the runner renders the single visible Refresh Activity panel below the browser viewport and the underlying dashboard omits its panel. After refresh the runner disappears and the dashboard panel returns, so exactly one panel is composed and visible at all times.
- Android Myntra readiness accepts a non-loading `myntra.com/gold-coin` page only after its visible text contains both the Gold Coin catalogue label and a positive `N items` count. It does not depend on the unstable private `window.__myx` state.
- After successful Android Amazon, Flipkart, or Myntra catalogue merges, both Refresh All and Refresh Selection send every database record absent from that accepted catalogue identity set through a sequential, paced follow-up using the active store WebView's cookies and referer. Myntra uses `/gateway/v2/product/<id>`; Amazon and regular Flipkart use their canonical product pages because their desktop contracts have no stable product API. A positive returned price updates the existing product to `live`; explicit stock/removal/HTTP-404 evidence marks it `unavailable`; blocked, timeout, and ambiguous responses preserve existing values/status. AJIO intentionally has no post-catalogue product fallback while its access-denied behavior is under observation. This follow-up does not run when a catalogue master itself fails or is blocked.
- Flipkart `marketplace=HYPERLOCAL`/Minutes records retain their location-specific product flow and are excluded from the generic regular-Flipkart post-catalogue fallback.
- Android post-catalogue Amazon and regular Flipkart product-page checks use retailer-specific HTML price extraction matching their desktop parser patterns. Hyperlocal/Minutes remains excluded until its multi-step saved-location WebView flow is implemented.
- A full Android bullion refresh combines three direct-HTTP sources with browser-rendered Tanishq. Market progress reports all four sources while Tanishq is active; a Tanishq-only refresh remains a one-source operation.
- Android Refresh Activity is Room-backed and retained under Watchlist with full console source/line, main-frame, HTTP, SSL, renderer, readiness, coverage, and completion diagnostics. Its Copy output includes a short session ID, explicit background/optional-Browser mode, target/store URL queue and concurrency, URL progress, localhost bridge HTTP status/accepted/bounded-body or network failure diagnostics, unique accepted coverage, structured bridge rejection counts, and final per-store outcome or cancellation/late-payload rejection evidence. Retailer console source URLs are compacted and identical known retailer bootstrap exceptions are retained once per navigation as warnings so logs remain readable; true bridge/navigation/readiness/HTTP/SSL/renderer failures remain errors. Refresh requests are typed as All, current Selection, Stale only, or one-store retry; target stores come only from visible products, and an empty scope closes immediately. Each refresh registers its UUID with allowed stores before the WebViews start, injects it into all localhost bridge POSTs, and cancels it only on terminal completion, explicit cancellation, or screen disposal so delayed or wrong-store payloads cannot mutate Room. At most two store WebViews run concurrently, AJIO URLs stay serial, and each WebView waits until its matching URL index is created before navigation, preventing old WebView reuse/duplicate URL loads during recomposition. Product/Tanishq renderers stay in a 1dp host while the permanent Browser dashboard is optional; normal Back/tab navigation does not cancel or recreate active jobs. Bridge/archive product URLs require HTTPS plus ownership by the claimed retailer; malformed present coupon, grams, and karat values are rejected, and a bridge record without current grams/karat remains `unverified` rather than `live`. Product price history uses an `ON DELETE CASCADE` Room foreign key. Deal Radar requires a recent, metadata-complete 22K/24K live observation and excludes implausibly cheap per-gram values. Bullion snapshots share a refresh timestamp for true blended trend points and enforce plausible rates through collection, import, and rendering. Desktop bullion history is seeded idempotently from packaged SQLite/WAL data. Product-history visualization remains pending.
- Android retailer WebView hosting (authoritative for `BrowserRefreshScreen`/`TanishqBrowserScreen`): each `StoreRefreshRunner` owns exactly one `AndroidView`, one `FrameLayout` and one `WebView` for its whole run, so AJIO walks all four URLs on the same WebView and its cookie/DOM/JS environment is not churned between URL indices; Tanishq likewise has exactly one WebView. Neither host is keyed on visibility or URL index, so opening Browser or advancing a URL never re-runs a factory or duplicates navigation. Activity/Compose recreation does destroy the host; a new WebView generation is created and `NavigationDecision` navigates the current URL exactly once on it. No WebView instance survives Activity recreation. While backgrounded the host is 1dp, pushed off-screen and clipped, and the WebView child keeps a `BrowserViewport` size derived from the current window (`414x896dp` only as a reported measurement fallback); while visible the same child switches to `MATCH_PARENT` through a LayoutParams change, never a recreation or reparent. `RetailerWebView.navigate` returns `NavigationResult.LoadStarted(token)`/`LoadFailed(reason)`; the returned token is the only navigation-start token, and the stall watchdog observes it.
- Android AJIO WebView policy uses the native System WebView UA rather than the shared macOS Chrome UA, uses `LOAD_DEFAULT`, and does not inject captured `plpRequestMobile`; the shared master derives its request from the current category URL. Known Access Denied/security/CAPTCHA pages terminate AJIO after the first confirmed block, preserve existing products/prices, and do not execute the master or retry immediately. Blocked is a distinct terminal refresh outcome, excluded from updated/partial counts, with `AJIO - Access blocked` user text and retained HTTP 403/Access Denied/Akamai diagnostics. The blocked tile provides an external `ACTION_VIEW` AJIO URL action for viewing only; it does not refresh, inject a master, or access browser session data. Physical same-device evidence shows real Chrome opens the exact filtered URL while System WebView can receive an Akamai HTTP 403, so changing the navigation URL/query is not an evidence-supported fix.
- Visible Browser refresh content is a single opaque overlay constrained below the 64dp top app bar and above the 62dp bottom navigation plus system navigation inset. It must not paint behind either fixed bar; moving the runner's composition slot would restart its WebView/session lifecycle.
- `src/app/server.js`: HTTP API/static server, in-memory state, scheduling, SSE clients, refresh orchestration, worker IPC, shutdown/restart.
- `src/storage/state-store.js`: loads and atomically writes authoritative JSON state split across `data/bullion.json` and `data/products/*.json`; supports legacy `data/state.json` migration.
- `src/storage/history-db.js`: mirrors current state and records product, bullion, and refresh history in `data/aurum.sqlite` using Node's SQLite API.
- `src/bullion/`: source definitions, retailer parsing, browser collection, and a forked worker.
- `src/product/stores/weight-parser.js`: shared weight and non-gold parsing rules.
- `src/product/stores/http-fast-path.js`: bounded speculative HTML fetch before browser rendering.
- `src/product/stores/page-pool.js`: persistent browser context/page reuse and idle-page cleanup.
- `src/product/stores/{ajio,amazon,flipkart,myntra}/`: each store owns `store.js` parsing/navigation, `collector.js` concurrency/runtime, and `worker.js` IPC cleanup. AJIO, Flipkart, and Myntra batch refreshes discover and refresh qualifying catalogue products through retailer listing data; unavailable catalogue transport preserves current values without opening PDPs. Single Retry stays targeted. Persisted `refreshMethod` distinguishes catalogue, API, HTTP, and browser results.
- AJIO direct-master discovery uses one unified script, `manual_js/ajio_gold_master.js`, across four configured filtered pages: Boys curated, Girls curated, Jewellery curated with 22K included, and Women category with 24K/999 facets, `nontransacted` cohort, and pincode `560048`. The original split scripts are preserved under `manual_js/backups/2026-08-30-unified-ajio/`; only the unified script is executable. Myntra, Flipkart, and Amazon retain their existing master URLs.
- `extension/content.js` is also an accepted-browser live-data bridge: on the reloaded AJIO/Myntra listing tabs it fetches their same-origin listing APIs, selectively enriches incomplete records through product JSON APIs, and posts live results to `/api/browser-bridge/products` on local ports 8787/8788. AJIO uses `/api/search` pagination and Myntra uses multi-sort boundary probes, matching the master extractors; this path does not load product pages.
- Every received bridge payload is preserved verbatim under `data/browser-bridge/` before normalization and can be downloaded as a JSON bundle at `/api/browser-bridge/raw`; Refresh Activity creates a Raw data download control for this exact received input.
- Each unfiltered Refresh All creates `data/browser-bridge/refresh-<timestamp>/` with `run.json` and `runner-results.json` from the direct four-master run. Bridge payload archives are still stored when `/api/browser-bridge/products` is called independently.
- Each Refresh All run folder also receives `runner-results.json` when automated listing scripts finish, including per-page navigation, retailer, bridge, and timeout diagnostics. The UI completion note updates with late runner errors when the global collection window ended first.
- `.github/STORE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT.md`: authoritative store-by-store map of active calls, fallbacks, dormant code, failure semantics, defaults, and dangerous edit areas. Read only the relevant section for store work.
- `.github/AJIO_PLP_FLOW_PLAN.md`: planning-only proposal for replacing automatic per-product AJIO refresh with one search-results-page collection. It contains live evidence, parser gaps, safeguards, rollout, tests, and unresolved decisions; it is not current production behavior.
- `src/common/browser.js`: shared Playwright launch/context/dialog/block detection.
- `src/common/environment.js`: centralized scraper environment configuration.
- `src/common/utils.js`: timeout, delay, number, and host-request helpers.
- `scratch/`: standalone tests, live probes, inspectors, normalization jobs, and one-off repairs; not production imports.
- `scratch/ajio-listing-extractor.js`: read-only browser canary for categories `830306012` and `830306009`. It paginates structured listings, enriches purity by facet membership, uses bounded `/api/p` JSON for unresolved exact qualifiers, never loads PDP documents, and writes only browser globals/download helpers. It is not production flow and does not persist Aurum data.
- `scratch/test-ajio-proposed-raw-visible.js`: visible persistent Firefox diagnostic for the proposed AJIO Girls search scope. It removes all proxy environment variables, captures a raw successful listing API response before running the master with bridge posting disabled, and never modifies Aurum state. The initial fresh-profile run received no successful listing API response within 30 seconds.
- `scratch/restore-ajio-plp-status.js`: one-off guarded recovery for previously successful AJIO PLP records after the blocked-run status regression; not a normal refresh command.
- `src/product/stores/ajio/browser-runtime.js`: production browser-side script installed automatically by the collector. Its observable DevTools state is `window.__aurumAjioListing.state`; the scratch extractor is not auto-executed.

## Data Flow

1. Server loads JSON state and initializes references to bullion/products.
2. API or scheduler starts bullion/product refresh work.
3. Server forks the relevant worker; workers send progress/results over IPC.
4. Collectors try eligible HTTP fast paths, then store-specific Playwright flows.
5. Server merges results while preserving stale values on failures, persists JSON, mirrors SQLite, records history, and broadcasts SSE updates.
6. Frontend consumes `/api/state`, progress/history endpoints, and `/api/events` with polling fallback.

## Frontend Execution Context

- `public/index.html` contains the complete desktop/mobile shell. `/` and `/mobile` load the same markup; `public/app.js` applies `body.mobile-mode` for the explicit `/mobile` route or a mobile-sized mobile user agent.
- `public/app.js` owns all rendering and interaction without a framework. State comes from `/api/state`; SSE `/api/events` updates are coalesced during refreshes, with 30-second REST polling only when SSE is unhealthy.
- Desktop products render table controls with `data-edit-id`, `data-delete-id`, and `data-retry-id`. Mobile cards render separate controls with `data-mobile-edit`, `data-mobile-delete`, and `data-mobile-retry` because desktop rows are not rendered in mobile mode.
- Delegated document handlers must accept both desktop and mobile dataset names and call APIs directly. Do not reintroduce synthetic clicks against desktop controls; those controls do not exist in the mobile DOM.
- Store tiles display global tracked counts for All/AJIO/Amazon/Flipkart/Myntra. Quick-filter chips display counts within currently selected stores plus active search and weight bounds, before the quick filter itself; Below bullion uses the product benchmark and Not live means every status except live.
- Delete is intentionally two-step: the first click stores `pendingDeleteId` for four seconds and shows confirmation; only the second click issues `DELETE /api/products/:id`.
- Retry issues one `POST /api/products/:id/retry`, marks the local product `checking`, starts live polling, then reloads state. The server currently performs this retry with a visible browser.
- `#restartButton` must have exactly one listener. It sends one `POST /api/restart`, preserves activity logs and current view state, then polls `load()` until the detached replacement backend process is reachable. The server has exactly one restart route, which closes workers and retained browser contexts, persists state, spawns a replacement Node process, then closes the old listener. It does not force a page reload or promise fresh frontend code.
- Refresh terminal lines persist in `sessionStorage` under `aurum-terminal-logs`. Consecutive duplicates are keyed by both `kind` and `message`; startup seeds the key from the last persisted line so reload restoration does not duplicate it while severity/status changes remain visible.
- Bullion trend state starts at `trendKarat = 24`. This declaration must exist before initial `load()`/`render()`; an undefined trend state rejects startup rendering before later delegated handlers can register.
- Service worker `public/sw.js` is network-first for non-API shell assets with cache fallback. Whenever `public/app.js` or `public/styles.css` changes, increment the matching asset query in `public/index.html`, both shell URLs in `public/sw.js`, and `cacheName` together. Current synchronized app revision: **v531**.
- Refresh Activity Clear removes terminal lines and resets its six displayed counters to zero without touching tracked products or their statuses; the counters resume when the user starts another product refresh.
- Live benchmark card is intentionally similar to source rate cards: it uses the same two `.rate-value` price-row rhythm for 24K and 22K, with compact benchmark-only median-cleaned notes, range bars, and karat-specific low/high labels below each row. Keep 22K visible there; only its accent color differs.
- Bullion trend chart plots blended benchmark history, not per-source samples. It shows 24K and 22K blended benchmark lines on the same timestamp/date x-axis and price y-axis; the y-axis auto-ranges to 95% of the visible low and 105% of the visible high. The 24K/22K controls toggle each visible series, with at least one series kept visible; 22K uses the warm `--gold2` tone.
- Browser settings are end-to-end: `debugVisibleBrowser` forces a visible Firefox rendering pass for every bullion source; `productDebugVisibleBrowser` launches visible direct-master and targeted product contexts. A changed product visibility mode replaces the retained direct-master context on the next refresh, while the same mode reuses its warmed session. Visible direct-master tabs call `bringToFront()` after navigation, including the isolated AJIO category pages. `refreshBullionOnStart` refreshes all bullion sources at server start, and `refreshProductsOnStart` runs the same full direct-master product refresh as Refresh All. All four default false and persist through `/api/settings` into `data/bullion.json`.
- The attached `better ui_donot optmise/` folder is comparison/reference material, not an alternate runtime source. `public/` remains authoritative and should not be replaced wholesale.

### Frontend Validation

- Static: `node --check public/app.js && node --check public/sw.js`.
- Single restart listener: count `restartButton` click registrations and require exactly one.
- Mobile browser check on `/mobile`: open Watchlist; dispatch/click mobile Edit and verify `#editProductModal` opens; intercept Retry and require one POST; first Delete click must issue zero DELETE requests and show confirmation; intercept Restart and require one POST.
- SSE keeps a connection open, so browser navigation tests should wait for `domcontentloaded`, not `networkidle`.

## API Surface

- Read: `GET /api/state`, `/api/health`, `/api/events`, `/api/history/bullion`, `/api/history/products/:id`, `/api/products/progress`, `/api/bullion/progress`, `/api/proxy-auth`.
- Mutate: `POST /api/settings`, `/api/rates`, `/api/products`, `/api/products/bulk`, `/api/products/:id/retry`, `/api/refresh`, `/api/refresh/:source`, `/api/products/refresh`, `/api/restart`, `/api/proxy-auth`.
- Product item operations: `PATCH /api/products/:id`, `DELETE /api/products/:id`.
- Proxy credentials: `DELETE /api/proxy-auth`.
- Static routes: `/` and `/mobile` both serve `public/index.html`.

## Important Invariants

- JSON remains authoritative; SQLite is additive and must not become the sole state source without an explicit migration. Gold products live under `data/products/*.json`; explicit silver/platinum records live separately in `data/precious-metals.json` and are exposed as `preciousMetalProducts` in state responses.
- `public/` remains the single frontend implementation.
- Keep desktop and mobile product controls routed through the same direct delegated handlers; mobile cards cannot proxy to omitted desktop rows.
- Keep one restart listener and preserve reconnect-in-place behavior unless the backend restart contract is deliberately changed.
- Keep per-store workers isolated and always dispose persistent browsers on completion/signals.
- All-store refresh groups products by store and runs store workers in parallel up to `PRODUCT_STORE_PARALLELISM` (default 4); each store also uses its own internal concurrency. A single store failure is isolated and must not set global `running=false` while other workers continue.
- Unfiltered Refresh All runs four direct catalogue masters in parallel (`ajio.com`, `myntra.com`, `flipkart.com`, `amazon.in`) with `Promise.allSettled`. It maintains exactly four persistent Firefox product windows: one each for AJIO, Amazon, Flipkart, and Myntra. The AJIO window contains five persistent tabs for coins `830306009`, bars/coins `830306012`, Women Rings `830306004`, Women Necklaces & Pendants `830306003`, and Girls Fine Jewellery `830616`; no additional AJIO window is launched. Filtered/selected refreshes remain limited to the stores represented by their targets. There is no global 25/29/60-second snapshot deadline. Stores complete when their own master completes or encounters a real retailer/proxy error.
- Each direct master runs the corresponding `manual_js` listing extractor in its own persistent browser session through explicit awaited page-context `eval`, matching a DevTools paste, and returns catalogue payloads directly to the parent (`store`, `complete`, `products`, `catalogue`, `missing`, `runs`). The AJIO coin master classifies metal from its explicit product title before considering broad serialized listing/PDP metadata, preventing unrelated silver facet data from excluding a title-confirmed gold item. Its `ajioCoverageTable()` diagnostic distinguishes missing/failed expected search pages from reported-total versus unique-record gaps without triggering extra requests. The Amazon master sends any listing weight whose price is below `₹5,000/g` to its existing PDP parser and withholds it from the bridge when that verification cannot resolve the implausible weight.
- The AJIO child owns four persistent filtered-category tabs in one Firefox window. The first category uses the initial page; each further category is opened from it with `window.open(url, '_blank')`, while Firefox preferences direct target-blank pages into tabs. Every child tab waits `PRODUCT_AJIO_CHILD_PAGE_SETTLE_MS` (default 2500ms) then reloads once before its readiness/API probe. Each tab derives its exact request from the current URL, retries page-zero for up to 60 seconds, and passes page-zero/request state to the single unified master script. The unified script keeps only explicit genuine-gold records, skips explicit non-gold rows before PDP enrichment, and exports `ajioGold`, `ajioAllSearchResults`, and `ajioIncomplete` bindings.
- Direct masters now print explicit terminal diagnostics for verification: per-store start, full master URL list, per-link open/script-execution/completion/failure with durations and counts, and final store summary. Amazon waits up to 20 seconds for a search-result card before evaluating its master, preventing a successful evaluation against an empty initial DOM. The AJIO child additionally logs category-page readiness, each page-zero API probe URL/status, and whether `ajio_gold_master.js` executed or was skipped because readiness timed out. Each store run reuses one page for all configured links.
- Aurum uses Playwright Firefox exclusively. Direct masters create one temporary `/tmp/aurum-run-*` root per Aurum process, with isolated `ajio`, `amazon`, `flipkart`, and `myntra` profile subdirectories. These four persistent Firefox contexts are reused across every Refresh All in the same process, then the entire temporary tree is removed only after all contexts close during restart/shutdown. AJIO is isolated in `src/product/ajio-firefox-runtime.js`, a forked Node process whose environment deletes all upper/lower-case HTTP, HTTPS, ALL, and NO proxy variables before it launches the assigned `ajio` profile. AJIO retains four URL-bound tabs, snapshots each coin page's `plpRequestMobile` configuration before the next same-origin page can overwrite it, derives Women Fine Jewellery requests from their URLs when required, and retries each page-specific page-zero request for up to 60 seconds with backoff. Successful JSON responses and requests are assigned to `window.__AURUM_AJIO_PAGE0__` and `window.__AURUM_AJIO_REQUEST__`; the relevant master consumes them for its initial and subsequent pagination calls without re-reading shared local storage. A readiness timeout reports an explicit AJIO browser/API initialization failure. Set `PRODUCT_AJIO_MANUAL_DIAGNOSTIC=1` only to open all AJIO tabs without probes or master execution. Legacy AJIO/Myntra product routes and shared bullion browsers are also Firefox-only. `scripts/run.sh` installs Firefox, and no current source/runtime path selects Chromium or Google Chrome.
- Server startup safely removes only abandoned `/tmp/aurum-run-*` directories older than 24 hours. `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` await worker and direct-master browser disposal before the HTTP server closes, so normal shutdown removes the active temporary profile tree. `aurum-browser-profiles/` and its obsolete ZIP archive are not runtime inputs and are ignored/removed.
- Master navigation no longer does immediate `goto()` + `reload()`; it now uses `goto()` and waits for DOM readiness before script execution to reduce request churn.
- Direct master `complete` now requires at least one catalogue/product record; a script run that returns zero rows is treated as incomplete/failure for refresh summary status.
- Direct-master refresh emits start, per-link completion/failure, merge, and fallback-skipped events into Refresh Activity. Each completed link reports products, catalogue records, and incomplete records; each merge reports received, updated, discovered, and skipped records.
- After all five masters settle, the parent merges their catalogue outputs. A successful direct master never triggers targeted store-worker refresh for its incomplete rows; the Women Rings script is the exception within its own bounded master execution, where it enriches only incomplete genuine-gold rows from serialized PDP option values. A failed master preserves batch catalogue records without opening PDPs. Targeted store-worker fallback is allowed only for a multi-product request that explicitly names product IDs and includes that failed store. Filtered/store-specific batch refreshes preserve existing records on a master failure.
- Any multi-product refresh, including Refresh selection and filtered store sets, uses direct catalogue masters for only the stores present in its selected products. Product-page fallback is restricted to selected products whose store master fails. A single product refresh remains the direct PDP route.
- New unfiltered refresh runs clear stale progress note/event metadata at start so previous-run PDP messages do not leak into the new run's initial progress payload.
- Aurum browser launches always use direct network. Direct masters, product workers, and bullion collection ignore `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `PRODUCT_MASTER_PROXY`, and saved proxy credentials; no browser launch is assigned a proxy server or injected credentials. The Settings proxy credential UI/API remains available for a future explicit user-prompt flow, but it does not configure any current browser runtime.
- On macOS, Save proxy also stores the ID/password in the OS Keychain service `aurum-proxy-credentials`; server startup restores it into runtime memory. Credentials are never written to Aurum JSON state, raw bridge archives, or project context/change files.
- If a retailer rejects the isolated automated browser context, Refresh All preserves its existing records, opens no product pages for that store, and reports the captured per-store runner error in the completion note. AJIO's automated `/api/search` can be blocked even when an accepted user tab returns 200.
- `public/app.js` must send an empty payload for the default Refresh All button. Sending the entire list as `productIds` changes it into a targeted refresh and bypasses the browser-bridge session.
- Parent refresh progress is monotonic and capped to each store's tracked target. Catalogue collectors report unique observed product counts, not reset-prone page/offset counters.
- AJIO, regular Flipkart, and Myntra batch/automatic refresh use persistent-browser catalogue data to discover gold products; Flipkart Minutes stays on its original per-product location-aware browser flow. Every single-product Retry is explicitly targeted and retains its product-page/API route rather than running catalogue discovery. Use `.github/STORE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT.md` for exact lifecycle and rollback controls.
- Amazon and regular Flipkart direct catalogue masters do not submit a pincode or treat a listing card as delivery confirmation. Flipkart Minutes and its targeted product route retain their separate location-aware behavior.
- Store refresh errors preserve existing prices as stale rather than deleting useful state.
- A successful catalogue master marks only current matching, qualifying retailer records `live`. Historical records absent from its current catalogue remain `stale` (or `unverified` without a usable price); absence is not positive evidence of availability or freshness.
- AJIO product-page fallback preserves any valid last-known price as `stale` on worker/network/parser failure. It must not convert a retained value to `failed`; a historic code-130 worker interruption incorrectly did so for 35 products and was repaired to stale with `scratch/restore-interrupted-ajio-statuses.js`.
- Flipkart URL slugs such as `0-05-g` mean `0.05g`, not `0.5g`. Raw browser bridge records may omit grams; shared URL parsing resolves those records. Thirteen historical `0-05-g` values were corrected from `0.5g` to `0.05g` with `scratch/fix-flipkart-decimal-weights.js`. Flipkart bridge URLs strip volatile `iid`, `ssid`, `ov_redirect`, and `store` tracking parameters while retaining the stable `pid` and `marketplace=FLIPKART`; `scratch/normalize-flipkart-urls.js` repaired 480 persisted links.
- Normal batch refreshes must not pre-mark AJIO, regular Flipkart, or Myntra catalogue records as `checking`; when their separate worker session is blocked, retain the confirmed `live` status and record the failure only as `lastAttemptError`. Flipkart Minutes remains on the original per-product path and is marked `checking` only while its own page is refreshing.
- `unavailable` requires explicit stock/removal or non-gold evidence. AJIO ambiguity without a current price uses neutral `unverified`; known-price ambiguity uses stale. `failed` is reserved for actual processing failures.
- `live` is freshness, not general availability. `loadState()` changes a successfully priced product to `stale` when `lastLiveAt` is older than 30 minutes; stale products may still be available and retain their last-known price.
- Worker timeout/network ambiguity without a usable price is `unverified`, including Myntra. Do not use `unavailable` unless there is explicit stock/removal/non-gold evidence.
- Server startup re-extracts product weight from names/URLs and must pass it through `normalizeGoldWeight(..., product.price)` before comparing it with stored/manual weight. Raw extraction can misread retailer title errors such as `500 g` for a ₹9,490 coin that is actually 500 mg.
- Product deduplication uses store-aware canonical URLs. Regular Flipkart products deduplicate by `pid` with `marketplace=FLIPKART`, ignoring session/tracking parameters such as `iid` and `ssid`; Flipkart Minutes retains its `pid`, `marketplace=HYPERLOCAL`, and optional `shopId` location identity.
- `manuallyEditedAt` protects manual weights from smaller parsed values during startup reconciliation. Correct bad manual values through the product PATCH API; otherwise an exaggerated title token can overwrite the correction on restart.
- Below-24K products remain excluded from 24K deal comparisons and refresh less frequently unless manually requested.
- Startup refresh settings are opt-in. When enabled, server startup runs forced bullion first, then full product refresh second; `AUTO_REFRESH_ON_START=1` remains a backward-compatible bullion-only override.
- Mobile user-agent detection includes Android browsers even though no native Android app exists.
- Runtime proxy values may be sensitive; never log or persist credentials in context/change files.

## Configuration Groups

- Server/schedule: `PORT`, `HOST`, `AUTO_REFRESH_ON_START`, persisted startup settings, `BULLION_INTERVAL_MIN`, `SUB24K_REFRESH_MULTIPLIER`.
- Browser: `BROWSER_USER_AGENT`, `BULLION_BROWSER`, and visibility controls. Proxy environment variables are ignored by Aurum browser launches.
- Bullion: `BULLION_*` timeout, retry, source, and concurrency variables.
- Products: `PRODUCT_*` store concurrency, worker timeout, browser launch, page readiness, page pool, HTTP fast path, and store parallelism variables.
- AJIO lifecycle: `PRODUCT_AJIO_BROWSER_SUCCESS_LIMIT`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_BROWSER_FAILURE_LIMIT`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PAGE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_CHILD_PAGE_SETTLE_MS` (default 2500), `PRODUCT_AJIO_403_COOLDOWN_MS`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_BULK_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- AJIO PLP: `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_FLOW`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_CATEGORIES`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_REQUEST_DELAY_MS`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_DETAIL_LIMIT`, `PRODUCT_AJIO_PLP_MINIMUM_COVERAGE`.
- Myntra PLP: `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_FLOW`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_ROWS`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_MAX_REQUESTS`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_SEARCH_CONCURRENCY`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_DETAIL_LIMIT`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_DETAIL_CONCURRENCY`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_REQUEST_DELAY_MS`, `PRODUCT_MYNTRA_PLP_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- Flipkart PLP: `PRODUCT_FLIPKART_PLP_FLOW`, `PRODUCT_FLIPKART_PLP_MAX_PAGES`, `PRODUCT_FLIPKART_PLP_REQUEST_DELAY_MS`.
- Product-store Playwright launches use direct network; do not record proxy credentials in project files.
- Browser bridge: reload the unpacked extension and the retailer listing tabs while Aurum runs at `http://localhost:8787` or `http://localhost:8788`. Only records returned by retailer APIs are marked `live`; blocked worker sessions do not substitute local history.

## Validation And Constraints

- Offline parser checks: `node scratch/test-parsing.js && node scratch/test-all-cases.js`.
- Full JavaScript syntax and shell syntax commands are in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- Runtime health endpoint: `/api/state` or `/api/health` on the selected port.
- Live scraper checks require browser/network access and can take minutes.
- README version notes are historical. When a release note conflicts with current source, source plus `.github/STORE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT.md` controls and both context files must be updated after behavior changes.
- The directory currently has no `.git`; rely on targeted reads, the agent ledger, and external archives for recovery.
